articles.title: How to Free Up SSD Space for 100 GB Games
articles.excerpt: New games regularly need 100 GB or more on an SSD. See what is using your space, move games between drives without re-downloading, and what consoles allow.
articles.hero_image_alt: Storage bar showing a 115 GB game needing free space on an SSD

body.text: Big releases now regularly need more than 100 GB on an SSD. Modern Warfare 4 lists 115 GB and Ace Combat 8 lists 125 GB. The fastest way to make room is to **move games you are not playing to another drive**, which avoids downloading them again later.
First, see what is using the space
**On Windows:** open Settings, then System, then Storage. Windows shows how much space apps, temporary files and other categories are using.
**On Steam:** open Settings, then Storage. You get a list of installed games on each drive, sorted by size.
Start with the largest items. Removing one 100 GB game you finished months ago does more than an hour of clearing small files.
Move games to another drive
In Steam's Storage settings you can select installed games and **move them to another drive** without re-downloading. You can add a second drive there as a new library location first.
The Xbox app on PC also lets you choose which drive a game installs to, and move installed games between drives.
Keep in mind:

items: **Games that require an SSD should stay on an SSD.** Moving one to a hard drive can cause long loads and stutter, or stop it from running.
**Older and smaller games are good candidates** for a hard drive.

body.text: Uninstall what you are not playing
Your purchases stay in your library, and cloud saves keep your progress for games that support them. Check that a game shows cloud saves before removing it if the save matters to you.
Clear temporary files
In Windows Storage settings, open **Temporary files** and remove what you do not need. Read the list before confirming: the Downloads folder can appear there, and you may not want it emptied.
PlayStation 5

items: **PS5 games must run from the console's internal SSD or an M.2 SSD** installed in the expansion slot.
A USB extended storage drive can **store** PS5 games to free up space, but they have to be moved back before you can play them.
PS4 games can be played directly from USB extended storage.

body.text: Xbox Series X|S

items: Games optimized for Series X|S must run from the **internal SSD or a Storage Expansion Card**.
A USB drive can **store** those games, and can run older Xbox One, Xbox 360 and original Xbox games directly.

body.text: How much free space to aim for
Keep more free than the install size. Launchers need working room while unpacking and patching, and updates for large games are often tens of gigabytes.
If you are preparing for a specific launch, read [how preloading works on each platform](/install/how-game-preloading-works).
Quick answers
Can I move a Steam game without downloading it again?
Yes. Use Settings, then Storage, select the game and move it to another drive.
Can I run PS5 games from a USB drive?
No. You can store them there, but they run only from the internal SSD or an M.2 SSD.
Will uninstalling a game delete my save?
Not if the game uses cloud saves and they have synced. Check before uninstalling.

articles.title: How Game Preloading Works on Steam, Xbox, PlayStation and Battle.net
articles.excerpt: Preloading downloads a game before release so it is ready at unlock. How it works on each platform, and why it still needs time on launch day.
articles.hero_image_alt: Diagram of a game download finishing before release day and unlocking at launch

body.text: Preloading means downloading a game's files before its release date, so the game is ready to start when it unlocks. You usually need to have bought or pre-ordered the game, or have a subscription that includes it.
What preloading does and does not do

items: **It downloads the files early.** The large download happens days before launch, not at the moment everyone else starts.
**It does not let you play early.** The files stay locked until the official unlock time.
**It may not be the final version.** Many games get a day-one patch, so expect another download at launch.

body.text: Steam
When a publisher opens preloading, the install button appears on the game's page in your Library. The files are downloaded in an encrypted form.
At release, Steam has to **decrypt and unpack** those files before the game will start. On a slow drive this can take a while for a 100 GB game, so do not expect to be playing in the first minute.
Not every Steam game offers a preload. It is the publisher's choice.
Xbox consoles and the Xbox app on PC
Xbox calls this **pre-install**. It is available for pre-ordered games and for many upcoming Game Pass games.
Find the game in the Store or the Game Pass section and choose to pre-install it. You can also start the download remotely from the Xbox mobile app.
PlayStation 5
On PS5, pre-ordered digital games can **pre-download automatically** shortly before release. In many cases this starts about two days ahead.
For it to work without you touching the console, automatic downloads need to be enabled and the console needs to stay in rest mode with an internet connection.
Battle.net
In the Battle.net app, a pre-load option appears on the game's page once the publisher opens it. Call of Duty and Blizzard games commonly use this.

Modern Warfare 4 opens PC preloading on October 15, eight days before launch. See [Modern Warfare 4's PC requirements, preload time and install size](/requirements/modern-warfare-4-pc-requirements-preload).
For GTA 6 on PS5, [GTA 6 release time by time zone](/releases/gta-6-release-time-by-time-zone) converts the reported unlock moment into Eastern, Central, Mountain and Pacific time.
Before you preload

items: **Check free space first.** A download fails or pauses if the drive fills up. Some launchers also need extra temporary space while unpacking.
**Install to an SSD when the game requires one.** Many new games do.
**Use a wired connection for very large games** if you can.

body.text: If you are short on space, read [how to free up SSD space for large games](/guides/free-up-ssd-space-for-large-games).
Quick answers
Can I play a preloaded game early?
No. The files unlock at the official release time.
Why is my preloaded game still installing on launch day?
The launcher has to decrypt and unpack the files, and there may be a day-one patch.
Do all games offer preloading?
No. The publisher decides whether to offer it and when it starts.

If you already own it on Steam

items: **Back up your saves.** Large updates can change how worlds and characters are stored.
**Check the developer's 1.0 notes for save compatibility.** We have not seen Keen Games confirm how existing early access worlds carry over, so do not assume either way.

body.text: What was added during early access

A cosmetic transmog layer
Playable instruments

Xbox players have to wait

Still to be confirmed

articles.title: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve Install Size and PC Requirements
articles.excerpt: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve needs 125 GB on an SSD and Windows 11 on PC. Minimum and recommended specs, what the targets mean, and Denuvo status.
articles.hero_image_alt: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve official screenshot

body.text: **Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve needs 125 GB of storage on an SSD**, and the PC version lists **Windows 11** as its only supported operating system. The game released on October 2, 2026 for PC, PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
At a glance
PC system requirements
These are Bandai Namco's official PC specs, as reported by DSOGaming.
What these targets mean
Two details are easy to miss:

items: **Both targets use upscaling.** The recommended tier is 1080p at 60 FPS on Medium with an upscaler turned on. It is not a native 1080p target, and no official tier is given for 1440p or 4K.
**32 GB of RAM is recommended.** That is double what most 2026 releases ask for. With 16 GB you meet the minimum tier, which targets 30 FPS on Low.

body.text: If your PC sits between the two tiers, expect to mix Low and Medium settings to hold 60 FPS.
Windows 10 is not listed

Both tiers list Windows 11 64-bit only. Bandai Namco has not listed Windows 10 as supported, so Windows 10 players should treat the game as unsupported on their system until the publisher says otherwise.
Storage: plan for more than 125 GB
The game must be installed on an SSD. Keep extra room free for patches and shader data on top of the 125 GB install.

If you need to make space, our guide covers [how to free up SSD space for large games](/guides/free-up-ssd-space-for-large-games), including moving other games to a second drive without re-downloading them.
Quick answers
How big is Ace Combat 8 on PC?
125 GB, on an SSD.
Does Ace Combat 8 run on Windows 10?
Only Windows 11 is listed in the official requirements.
Does Ace Combat 8 use Denuvo?
Yes, according to DSOGaming's report on the official specs.
How much RAM does Ace Combat 8 need?
16 GB minimum and 32 GB recommended.
Sources

items: [DSOGaming, Ace Combat 8 official PC requirements and Denuvo](https://www.dsogaming.com/news/ace-combat-8-wings-of-theve-gets-official-pc-requirements-will-have-denuvo/)

articles.title: How to Check TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot on Windows Before a Game Launch
articles.excerpt: Some PC games now require TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot. Check both in two minutes with built-in Windows tools, and what to do if either one is off.
articles.hero_image_alt: Checklist showing TPM 2.0, UEFI mode and Secure Boot as the three things to check

body.text: Some PC games refuse to start unless **TPM 2.0** and **Secure Boot** are enabled, because their anti-cheat relies on them. You can check both in about two minutes with tools already built into Windows.
Modern Warfare 4 is one example. See its [PC requirements, preload time and install size](/requirements/modern-warfare-4-pc-requirements-preload).
Check TPM 2.0

items: Press **Windows + R**, type **tpm.msc** and press Enter.
Look at **Status**. It should say the TPM is ready for use.
Look at **Specification Version** under TPM Manufacturer Information. It should say **2.0**.

body.text: If the window says a compatible TPM cannot be found, the TPM is most likely switched off in your motherboard settings. That is common on PCs built by their owners.
Check Secure Boot

items: Press **Windows + R**, type **msinfo32** and press Enter.
Find **BIOS Mode**. It should say **UEFI**.
Find **Secure Boot State**. It should say **On**.

body.text: What your results mean

rows: Turn on Secure Boot in your firmware settings.
Turn on the firmware TPM in your firmware settings.
Your Windows drive needs converting first. See below.

body.text: Turning them on

Both settings live in your motherboard's firmware settings, often still called the BIOS. You reach them by pressing a key such as Delete or F2 while the PC starts. The exact menu names differ between manufacturers.

items: **TPM:** on Intel systems the setting is usually called **PTT** (Platform Trust Technology). On AMD systems it is usually called **fTPM**.
**Secure Boot:** usually found under a Boot or Security menu.

body.text: Change one setting at a time and check that Windows still starts normally.
If BIOS Mode says Legacy
Secure Boot needs UEFI mode, and UEFI needs your Windows drive to use the GPT partition style. A PC in Legacy mode usually has an MBR drive.
Windows includes a tool called **MBR2GPT** that can convert the drive without erasing it, but this is the one step here that can stop Windows from starting if it goes wrong.

items: **Back up your important files first.**
Follow Microsoft's own instructions for MBR2GPT and for your motherboard.
If you are not comfortable with this, ask someone who is. Do not rush it on launch day.

body.text: Do this before launch day
Check now, not when the game unlocks. Changing firmware settings is quick when it goes well and slow when it does not, and launch day is a bad time to find out.
Quick answers
How do I know if I have TPM 2.0?
Run tpm.msc and check that Specification Version says 2.0.
Is it safe to turn on Secure Boot?
On a PC already in UEFI mode it is normally a simple switch. On a PC in Legacy mode you need to convert the drive first, so back up before you start.
Will enabling TPM slow down my games?
No. It is a security feature and does not change game performance.

body.text: **Star Wars: Galactic Racer launches on October 6, 2026.** On Steam the Standard Edition costs **$59.99** and the Deluxe Edition costs **$79.99**, and the PC version needs **50 GB on an SSD**.

Editions and prices

Pre-purchasing either edition adds an exclusive repulsorcraft livery and an exclusive multiplayer player banner.
Minimum PC requirements
From the game's Steam page:
The recommended tier is listed on the Steam page too. Check it there before buying if you plan to play above 1080p.

When does Star Wars: Galactic Racer come out?
October 6, 2026.

$59.99 for Standard and $79.99 for Deluxe on Steam in the US.
How big is Star Wars: Galactic Racer on PC?
50 GB, and an SSD is required.

articles.title: Modern Warfare 4 PC Requirements, Preload Time and Install Size
articles.excerpt: Modern Warfare 4 needs 115 GB of SSD space, TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot on PC. PC preload starts October 15 at 9 AM PT and the game launches October 23.
articles.hero_image_alt: Preload graphic: Modern Warfare 4 PC preload opens October 15 at 9 AM PT for digital pre-purchases, 115 GB SSD required, TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot required on PC
articles.hero_image_caption: Graphic: Preload. Source: Call of Duty blog

body.text: **Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches on October 23, 2026, and PC preloading begins on October 15 at 9 AM PT.**   On PC it needs 115 GB of SSD space, TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot.

Every spec, date and requirement on this page comes from the Call of Duty blog's PC post of September 29, 2026, unless another Call of Duty post is named.  The time conversions in the second table are our own arithmetic.
Key dates

rows: October 15, 9 AM PT, for players who pre-purchase digitally on PC
Starts October 16, for digital pre-orders of the Standard Digital or Vault Edition
PC only (Call of Duty blog PC post)
Xbox on PC, Battle.net and Steam

body.text: The Call of Duty pre-order guide lists the October 23, 2026 launch for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Nintendo Switch 2; the midnight local time above comes from the PC post.
PC preload time in other time zones

headers: Preload opens (our conversion of 9 AM PT)

body.text: We converted 9 AM PT ourselves, using the summer time offsets shown in the table, which apply in the US and UK on October 15, 2026. The Call of Duty blog's PC post states the preload time as 9 AM PT; the other times are our conversion.
PC system requirements

rows: AMD Ryzen 5 1400 or Intel Core i5-6600
AMD Ryzen 5 3600 or Intel Core i7-8700K
AMD Ryzen 7 3700X or Intel Core i7-10700K
Radeon RX 470, GeForce GTX 970 / 1060 or Intel Arc A580
Radeon RX 6600 XT, GeForce RTX 3060 Ti or Intel Arc B580
Radeon RX 9070 XT or GeForce RTX 5070 Ti

body.text: The blog says these specs are valid for launch and may be updated in the future.
TPM 2.0, Secure Boot and AVX

The Call of Duty blog says TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot are required to play Modern Warfare 4 on PC.  It also says only Intel and AMD processors with the AVX instruction set are supported at this time.  Our guide shows [how to check TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot on Windows](/guides/check-tpm-secure-boot-windows) before preload day.
Install size and storage

The Minimum, Recommended and Ultra specs in the blog's PC post each list 115 GB with an SSD required.    The blog adds that additional storage space may be required for mandatory game updates, so leave room beyond 115 GB.  If space is tight, see [how to free up SSD space for large games](/guides/free-up-ssd-space-for-large-games).
Before preload day: checklist

items: Pre-purchase digitally on PC if you want to preload: the blog ties PC preloading to digital pre-purchases.
Free more than 115 GB on an SSD.
Turn on TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot.
Check your CPU is an Intel or AMD processor with AVX.
Preloading opens October 15 at 9 AM PT.  For how preloading works on each store, read [how game preloading works](/install/how-game-preloading-works).

body.text: PC features listed on the Call of Duty blog

items: More than 800 customization options across graphics, gameplay, input devices, interface and more.
Ray tracing in Campaign, Multiplayer and DMZ.
A range of upscaling and frame generation technologies, including AMD FSR Redstone.
A built-in benchmark tool.
Advanced Shader Delivery, which provides precompiled shaders ahead of time.
HDR10+.

articles.title: GTA 6 Install Size and Preload: What Is Confirmed and What Is Not
articles.excerpt: GTA 6 preloading starts November 12, 2026 for digital pre-orders. Rockstar has not announced the install size. How much space to plan for.
articles.hero_image_alt: GTA 6 status: release November 19, preload November 12, install size and unlock time not announced

body.text: **GTA 6 preloading starts on November 12, 2026, one week before the November 19 launch.** Rockstar has **not announced the install size**, so every number you see quoted today is an estimate.
What is confirmed
How big will GTA 6 be?
Nobody outside Rockstar knows yet. SVG's launch guide notes that estimates range from 150 GB to far higher, and treats 200 to 300 GB as the top of reasonable speculation.

For comparison, other big games this season list between 115 GB and 125 GB. A larger install for GTA 6 would not be surprising, but treat any exact figure as a guess until the PlayStation Store or Xbox Store shows one. That usually happens when preloading opens.
How to prepare your console now
You do not need the exact number to get ready.

items: **Check your free space today.** On PS5, open Settings and then Storage. On Xbox, open My games and apps and then Manage.
**Aim to have at least 200 GB free** before November 12. If the game turns out smaller, you have lost nothing.
**Move or delete games you have finished.** See [how to free up SSD space for large games](/guides/free-up-ssd-space-for-large-games) for what PS5 and Xbox allow on external drives.
**On Xbox Series S, plan carefully.** A 512 GB console may need most of its drive cleared, or a Storage Expansion Card.

body.text: How the preload will work
Preloading applies to digital pre-orders. Once it opens, the download starts from the store page or your library, and on PS5 it can begin automatically if automatic downloads are switched on.
The game will still be locked until the launch time. For how this works on each console, read [how preloading works on Steam, Xbox, PlayStation and Battle.net](/install/how-game-preloading-works).
We will update this page
When Rockstar or the console stores publish the install size and unlock time, both will be added here.

Meanwhile, the PS5 unlock times reported from PlayStation Store listings, which do not come from a Rockstar announcement, are converted to Eastern, Central, Mountain and Pacific time in [GTA 6 release time by time zone](/releases/gta-6-release-time-by-time-zone).
Quick answers
How big is GTA 6?
Not announced. Published figures are estimates.
When can I preload GTA 6?
From November 12, 2026 with a digital pre-order.
Is GTA 6 on PC?
No PC version has been announced. It launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
Sources

items: [IBTimes UK, GTA 6 release date, preload time, price, editions and platforms](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/gta-6-release-date-pre-load-time-price-editions-platforms-confirmed-rockstar-1819557)

articles.title: How Long Will a Game Download Take? Mbps, GB and Install Time Explained
articles.excerpt: Estimate the transfer time from your actual download speed, then allow separately for unpacking, verification and updates.
articles.hero_image_alt: How Long Will a Game Download Take? Mbps, GB and Install Time Explained — official Supergiant Games / Steam artwork

body.text: A 100 GB game and a 100 Mbps connection sound like matching numbers. They are different units: file sizes are usually shown in bytes, while connection speeds are usually shown in bits. Eight bits make one byte. A simple transfer estimate is size in decimal GB multiplied by 8,000, divided by speed in Mbps.
Use the speed you can actually sustain

Read the launcher’s download graph during a steady transfer. If it reports MB/s, multiply by eight to compare it with Mbps. Do not use a brief peak. A connection shared with streaming, a busy game server or weak Wi-Fi can all produce a lower sustained rate than the broadband package suggests.

These rounded examples assume a constant rate, decimal GB and no additional overhead. They are planning estimates, not promised completion times. Some launchers use binary units or show a compressed download that differs from the space needed after installation.
Download, install and unlock are separate steps

A finished transfer may still need to be written, unpacked or verified. A preload can also remain locked until the publisher’s release time. When the launcher reports little network activity but ongoing disk activity, another download speed test will not explain the delay.
Plan a launch-day buffer

items: Check free space on the installation drive before starting.
Start the download early enough to allow for a patch and verification.
Keep the device powered and avoid a scheduled sleep during the transfer.
Look for the launcher’s ready-to-play state rather than relying on the transfer percentage.

body.text: For a group session, tell friends when installation is complete rather than quoting the original estimate. If a transfer is unexpectedly slow, compare the launcher’s network and disk graphs first. You can then decide whether to investigate the connection or the installation drive.

articles.title: Game Broken After an Update? Verify Steam Files Before Reinstalling
articles.excerpt: A practical order for checking a failed update: finish the download, protect saves, verify installed files, then test a clean launch.
articles.hero_image_alt: Game Broken After an Update? Verify Steam Files Before Reinstalling — official FromSoftware, Inc., Bandai Namco Entertainment / Steam artwork
articles.hero_image_caption: Image: FromSoftware, Inc., Bandai Namco Entertainment / Steam

body.text: A failed launch after a patch does not automatically mean that the whole installation needs to be replaced. Missing or damaged game files are one possible cause. Steam has a built-in verification tool that compares the installed files with the game’s expected installation and can download replacements.
First confirm the update finished

Open Downloads and look for a queued transfer, a paused update or an ongoing installation step. Restarting the game while the launcher is still processing the patch can confuse troubleshooting. Note the error message and whether the game fails before the menu, while loading a save or only in a particular mode.
Protect what verification does not protect

Check the game’s own support page for its save location and mod instructions. Keep a separate copy of important local saves where the developer permits it. Verification is a tool for installation files; do not treat it as a way to recover progress or resolve a cloud-save conflict.
Run the installed-files check

items: Close the game.
In Steam Library, right-click its entry and open Properties.
Choose Installed Files, then Verify integrity of game files.
Allow verification and any replacement download to finish before testing.

body.text: Make the next test useful

Launch the game once with the normal supported configuration. If you use mods, follow the mod author’s removal procedure rather than deleting random folders. A patch can change what a mod expects even when Steam’s official files are intact. Record whether the same error occurs at the same point.

If verification passes and the failure remains, use the publisher’s known-issues page and support process. Share the exact message, game version and a short description of the test. Reinstalling is a later option, particularly for a large download, because it will not necessarily fix an account issue, incompatible mod or broken save.

articles.title: GTA 6 Release Time: When It Unlocks in Your Time Zone
articles.excerpt: Reported PlayStation Store listings put the GTA 6 unlock at midnight Eastern on November 19, 2026. US time zones, other regions and what is not confirmed.
articles.hero_image_alt: Table card of the reported GTA 6 PS5 unlock: 12:00 a.m. Eastern on Thursday November 19, 11 p.m. Central, 10 p.m. Mountain and 9 p.m. Pacific on Wednesday November 18, all one moment at 05:00 UTC
articles.hero_image_caption: Graphic: Preload, drawn from the reported unlock times on this page

body.text: **PlayStation Store listings reported on September 8, 2026 show GTA 6 unlocking in the United States at 12:00 a.m. Eastern on November 19, 2026, which is 9 p.m. Pacific on November 18.**  Rockstar has not announced an unlock time, and no Xbox time has been published.
The short version

items: **Reported US unlock (PS5 digital):** one moment for the whole country, 05:00 UTC on November 19, 2026.
**Where the time comes from:** regional PlayStation Store listings, as reported by two outlets on September 8, 2026.
**Not from Rockstar:** the report says none of the times come from a Rockstar announcement.
**Xbox:** Microsoft has not published unlock times.
**Could change:** the report says the listings could change before launch.

body.text: GTA 6 unlock time in each US time zone

The United States and Canada share a single window anchored to Eastern time, at 05:00 UTC on November 19, according to the September 8 report of the PlayStation Store listings.  That means the game does not unlock at midnight in every US time zone: the further west you are, the earlier in the evening of November 18 it is reported to open.
The rows below are our conversions of that one reported 05:00 UTC moment into US clock times. They are not separate listings.

Source for the 05:00 UTC window: PlayStation Store listings as reported by God is a Geek on September 8, 2026.  A second outlet, MP1st, reported the same day that the US and Canada share a UTC-5 window with Colombia, Ecuador, Panama and Peru.
Reported unlock times by region

In total the report counts 63 countries and regions in 15 windows, and outside North America they follow local midnight on November 19 rather than one global moment.  The table gives the windows the report names. The Eastern column is our conversion.
All rows are PlayStation Store listings as reported on September 8, 2026.   New Zealand is the earliest window the report names.
What is not confirmed

items: **Any time from Rockstar.** The times come from store listings, not an announcement.  One of the two reports credits Rockstar in its introduction and the PlayStation Store in its body, so treat headlines that say "Rockstar confirms" with care.
**Xbox Series X|S.** No Xbox unlock time has been published.
**Disc copies.** The reported times apply to the PS5 digital version only.
**Whether the listings still say the same thing.** They were reported on September 8, 2026 and could change.

**Changing your console region to start early.** One outlet says Xbox players can switch region to New Zealand and cites no source for it.  With no Xbox times published, there is nothing to show it works, and this page does not recommend it.

body.text: What to do before launch night

items: **Use your own time zone's row, not midnight.** In Central, Mountain and Pacific time the reported unlock falls on the evening of November 18.
**Check the store page again in launch week.** The listed time is the one that counts, and the report says it could change.

**Download ahead of time if you can.** The same report expects preloading to begin around November 12.  Our [GTA 6 install size and preload page](/install/gta-6-install-size-preload) covers how much space to plan for.
**On Xbox, wait for an official time.** None has been published.

body.text: Getting ready to download? [GTA 6 install size and preload: how to prepare](/install/gta-6-install-size-preload) covers how much space to clear, and [how preloading works on each platform](/install/how-game-preloading-works) explains what the early download does and does not do.
We will update this page when Rockstar, PlayStation or Xbox publishes an official unlock time.
